stem: Which statement best describes a key difference between juvenile dermatomyositis and adult dermatomyositis?

options.text: It does not affect the skin in children
It is not associated with malignancy in children
It causes muscle hypertrophy instead of weakness
It only affects the distal muscles in children
It usually presents with isolated joint swelling only

explanation: Juvenile dermatomyositis is not associated with malignancy in children. Unlike adult dermatomyositis, which may signal an underlying cancer, the paediatric form is typically an idiopathic inflammatory myopathy without a cancer association.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because juvenile dermatomyositis commonly has characteristic skin findings such as a heliotrope rash and Gottron papules.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because juvenile dermatomyositis is generally not linked to an underlying malignancy in children, unlike adult dermatomyositis.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because dermatomyositis causes proximal muscle weakness, not muscle hypertrophy.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the muscle weakness is typically proximal rather than limited to distal muscles.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because the condition is a myositis with skin involvement, not an isolated arthritis or joint-swelling disorder.

source.hint: Think about the presence or absence of underlying cancer.
